target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : ℕ) (N : S1 Bool Bool), N.D9 → S1.D5 T N d15 → N.d13 ≤ T
translation: Target defines (names, without proving or asserting) the following proposition: For every natural number T and every system N of type S1 Bool Bool—consisting of a finite type N.A1 of nodes, a state type N.A3 n for each node n, an initial global state N.a4 assigning a state in N.A3 n to each n, a transition rule N.a5 updating each node's state from the current global state and a Bool input, and an output function N.a6 mapping a global state to a Bool—if two hypotheses hold, then the number of nodes Fintype.card N.A1 is at most T (i.e., Fintype.card N.A1 ≤ T, written as an upper bound on the node count rather than a lower bound). The first hypothesis (N.D9) requires that the directed dependency relation on N.A1 has no nonempty directed cycles (including no self-loops): defining an edge m → n to hold when there exist two global states σ, σ' agreeing on every node k ≠ m and an input x : Bool such that N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x, there is no node n with a chain of one or more such edges from n back to n. (Note that this dependency test quantifies over all global states, not only reachable ones.) The second hypothesis (S1.D5 T N d15) requires that for every finite list xs of Booleans with xs.length ≤ T, running N from N.a4 by synchronously updating all nodes on each element of xs from left to right and then applying N.a6 yields the same Boolean output as the specific system d15 on xs; d15 is the single-node system (node type Unit, state type Bool) initialized to false that updates its state via state || x at each input x and outputs its final state (so d15 outputs true if xs contains at least one true, and false otherwise, including on the empty list). No requirements are placed on the finiteness or form of the individual node state types N.A3 n, on N.A1 being nonempty or free of unused/irrelevant nodes, or on the outputs of N for input lists of length strictly greater than T.

divergences.description: The inequality in the conclusion is reversed: Target asserts `N.d13 ≤ T` (at most T units, an upper bound) instead of `T ≤ N.d13` (at least T units, a lower bound). This contradicts both the author's claim ('has at least T units') and the source passages' point that feedforward/unrolled networks require many more neurons and grow large with the number of timesteps; as written, the statement is also false since arbitrarily many disconnected dummy units can be added to any feedforward implementation.

Target specializes and quantifies beyond what the source passages state: the passages make only qualitative claims that feedforward networks generally require many more neurons and that unrolling over 100 timesteps copies a network 100 times, whereas Target formulates an exact T-unit bound for one specific 1-unit Boolean latch (`d15`) over discrete steps (as acknowledged in the author's claim).

The formal framework idealizes neural networks as abstract synchronous state machines (`S1 Bool Bool`) with arbitrary (possibly infinite) per-unit state types, direct external input to every unit, and an arbitrary global readout; feedforwardness (`N.D9`) is defined via functional dependency across all global states (including unreachable ones) rather than synaptic/architectural acyclicity, and equivalence (`S1.D5 T`) is required for all input lengths ≤ T rather than only at step T.

judgement.summary: The Lean formalization is divergent because it reverses the inequality in the conclusion, asserting `N.d13 ≤ T` (an upper bound of at most T units) rather than the claimed lower bound of at least T units (`T ≤ N.d13`). Beyond this major error, the formalization introduces minor idealizations and specializes the sources' qualitative remarks to a specific Boolean 1-unit example.
